🌍 Iran calls on ITU to impartially assess damage to its communications infrastructure

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s Minister of Information and Communications Technology (ICT), Sattar Hashemi, has called for an impartial and comprehensive assessment of damage to the country’s communications and broadcasting infrastructure as well as technical recommendations for its reconstruction by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU).

On the sidelines of the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference 2026 (PP-26) in Doha, Hashemi met with Doreen Bogdan-Martin, Secretary-General of the ITU, stressing the need to expand technical and specialized cooperation between Iran and the organization.
​
He condemned the US and Israeli attacks on Iran and the damage inflicted on the country’s communication infrastructure, calling for the preservation of the ITU’s non-political and technical nature and international support for the protection of civilians.
​
Hashemi also called for follow-up on Iran’s request for an assessment of damage to its communications and information technology infrastructure and the provision of technical recommendations for reconstruction.
​
Referring to Iran’s analytical letter concerning the implementation of Resolution 1436, the minister called for a comprehensive, impartial, and evidence-based assessment of damage to the communications infrastructure of ITU member states, including Iran.
​
Hashemi further called for a technical assessment of damage to Iran’s telecommunications and broadcasting infrastructure and consideration of technical assistance and capacity-building support, stressing that an impartial approach was essential to preserving the credibility of the organization.
​
For her part, Bogdan-Martin underscored the importance of Iran’s active participation in the ITU’s activities, expressing the secretariat’s readiness to examine Iran’s request for an assessment of damage to its communications and broadcasting infrastructure through technical and expert channels.
​
Qatar hosts the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) in Doha from 9 to 27 November 2026. The Plenipotentiary Conference (PP) is the highest policy-making body of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), the United Nations agency for digital technologies.

“Dear United fans,

I've had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I'm incredibly grateful.

With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means.

It's different to anywhere else.

Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time.

It's a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored.

This is what inspired me every single day.

I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

We've had some great times this year and moments we'll all remember. The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time.

I just wanted to give you something back.

That love never dies.

I know we've not had the results lately, but you've shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

That means more than a win or two.

That's what makes you who you are.

That's why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.

A special thank you to my coaching staff. You gave me everything you had, every single day, and I couldn't have asked for any more. I'm incredibly grateful for your loyalty, hard work and support throughout.

To all the staff behind the scenes, thank you for everything you do for this football club. So much of your work goes unseen, but it never goes unappreciated.

And to the players, thank you for your efforts and the moments we've shared. I wish you all the very best for what's ahead.

I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change. I'll always be proud to have played my part and I'll always want the very best for it.

I'll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on”.
